status: approved P1 style (in game); revised 2026-09-30: back-view rout row added

anchor.desc: feet on native row 168 (same as warden.png); body centred at frameWidth/2

palette.swapHint: cloth1 = main garment (faction colour), paint = shield face (faction colour), cloth2 = hose/sleeves, cloth3 = hood/cap (secondary). Every material is its own ramp dark->light; a faction or kit-tier recolour is a straight colour-for-colour swap. Checked in code: no colour outside these ramps.

kitLayers.howToAddArmour: src/kits.py: set helmet / append to armour for a tier variant; new layer functions are registered in src/figure.py (HELMETS / ARMOUR / BODIES). Re-export regenerates the sheets.

nesMapping.paletteSource: reference/nes-palette.js (exact colours only; alpha 0 or 255; no anti-aliasing; dithering allowed)

skin.why: face T, shade a (standard NES skin pair); R only for the deepest crease. Not C: C is the jack/wood highlight.

hair.why: dark brown D; no highlight step, so hair and beard stay one flat mass like the warden walker hood.

cloth1.why: muted tan has no true NES match. O (ochre) is the closest perceptually, with C for quilting/highlight lines and D for shadow. Not T (reads as skin) and not Y/y (League gold).

cloth2.why: olive-grey hose/sleeves read as neutral grey S. NES has no desaturated olive; G/g are Covenant green. The 16-bit ramp was nudged greyer so the two tiers agree.

leather.why: boots, belt, gloves = D; the brightest leather step lifts to O only if a highlight is needed.

wood.why: shaft O (single 1 px line) with a K underside; C only for a glint.

metal.why: grey steps S/s/w. The kettle hat is drawn one step up (s body, S shade, w glint) so it stays the brightest thing on the walker, as in the 16-bit art.

paint.why: shield face E (orange-red), rim/shade R, glint a. The 16-bit paint ramp was changed from ochre to red-orange because ochre mapped to O, the same colour as the jack.

horse.why: red-chestnut coat = R (the NES "brown"), shade D, mane/tail D, hooves/socks K. The 16-bit coat was shifted from a brown bay to red-chestnut so it matches R; O/D were avoided because the road oxen are O/D and D would vanish on the D road.

outline.why: both outline rings become black K, as on the warden walker in 16-road-highland-moor.png. m (#940084) is the nearest hue to the magenta outer ring, but the road ground dither uses it, so an m outline would dissolve into the ground.

nesMapping.avoid: In this neutral scheme, keep G/g/l (Covenant green), P/p/L (Nightglass violet) and Y/y (League gold) free for faction versions. Faction swaps change cloth1 and paint only.
nesMapping.pickRule: labNearest is the raw nearest colour. Where the pick differs, it was chosen so the material still reads as the same material, e.g. skin mid-tones go a/T rather than D (brown dirt), and the jack mid-tone goes O rather than D/S (so it reads as tan cloth, not hair or steel).
nesMapping.dENote: dE is a Lab distance (nes.py) from the 16-bit colour to the picked NES colour; big values mean the NES palette has no close match.

nesCarryOver.walkerCanvas: 16x22 per frame, 4 frames (64x22 strip: A contact, B passing, C contact, D passing), facing right, feet on row 21, body centre x=8
mustCarryOver: bare head (no helmet) with brown hair and a short beard in D
tan quilted jack: O with vertical C quilting lines (O-O-C repeat), dark belt with a grey buckle
round red-orange shield on the rear arm (E face, R shade, a glint, grey boss, black rim)
short spear carried upright in the front hand, leaf blade s/w, butt clear of the ground
nesCarryOver.mustNotHappen: shield and jack must never share an NES colour (reason the 16-bit paint is red-orange).

notes.hit: frame 0 is a built-in brightness flash that stays inside the ramps (palette-swap safe).
notes.rout: both sheets, 4 frames. front: frame 0 = turning away, frames 1-3 = running away seen from behind. back: frame 0 = turning round, frames 1-3 = running toward the camera (screen-left). Play once, then loop frames 1-3 while the unit leaves.
notes.attack: thrust: front view toward bottom-left (the player), back view toward top-right; weapon foreshortened.
notes.death: the lowest body pixel of every death frame sits on the anchor (ground) row; dropped weapons lie on or above it.

revisions: 2026-09-30: death-row grounding fix: the lowest body pixel of every death frame now sits on the ground row (was measured from the in-hand weapon, bodies floated 2-6 px) (front+back death rows; every other row pixel-identical)
